visual.general_description: Vertical flowchart of six boxes: a practical algorithm for persistent age-inappropriate tachycardia in infants.
visual.detailed_description: Six stacked rectangular boxes joined by short downward arrows. Each has a bold heading and bullet lines. Box 1: "Age-inappropriate tachycardia → Confirm tachycardia at rest" with bullets about heart rate variation with rest, activity or crying and comparison with age-appropriate resting heart rate (typically ~100–160 bpm in young infants). Box 2: "Obtain a 12-lead ECG" with bullets asking whether the P wave can be identified and whether the QRS is narrow or wide. Box 3: "If the QRS complex is narrow and the P wave is indistinct → Consider administering adenosine/ATP" with bullets on rapid IV adenosine/ATP (e.g., 0.1–0.2 mg/kg adenosine; 0.2 mg/kg ATP) and unmasking of abnormal atrial waves. Box 4: "Chest X-ray, Echocardiography, BNP/NT-proBNP" with a bullet to evaluate cardiomegaly, LV size, wall motion, ejection fraction and structure. Box 5: "LV dysfunction present → Treat as TIC until proven otherwise" with bullets on prioritising rhythm control (e.g., synchronized cardioversion 0.5–1 J/kg [then 2 J/kg if needed] for AFL) plus heart failure therapy (acute: milrinone/diuretics; chronic: ACEi/β-blocker as appropriate) and excluding myocarditis, metabolic/mitochondrial/genetic causes. Box 6: "Follow -up: confirm recovery and detect recurrence" with bullets on serial echocardiography and Holter monitoring.
